content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I've finally tried uploading a program to my controller but ran into an issue. I have two different modules and used two computers: one with Windows 7 64-bit and the other with Windows XP 32-bit. Both are running [product_name] V6.1.12. When I attempt to upload, download, or toggle run/stop, the software hangs and I need to end it via task manager. The only constant is the USB cable. Has anyone experienced problems with these cables that could cause this, or should I consider other troubleshooting steps? Thanks for any advice.

Hello, To start, the current version of [product_name] does not officially support Windows 7. Try using the XP machine and, within the software, go to Tools/Option/interface automatic detection. Detection can take several minutes depending on the number of virtual COM-Ports. Eventually, one COM-Port should be identified. If automatic detection fails, open the Device Manager and look for a COM port entry related to Silicon Labs. Then manually select that COM-Port in the software and see if it operates correctly. Based on my experience, the USB cable for these controllers is usually reliable, so I doubt it's the source of the problem. Best regards, [user_name]

Hi [user_name], Thank you for your fast response. I wasn't aware the software didn't support Windows 7 when I first installed it. I've been using it for several months, but only now tried uploading and testing programs. I resolved the issue. The software was set to COM3 by default. When sending a program, a prompt appeared advising me to check connections or retry. Using automatic detection found COM1, but it kept crashing. Checking Device Manager revealed the correct port was COM8. Manually selecting that port fixed the problem. Interestingly, after fixing it, everything worked fine on both the XP and Windows 7 machines. Thanks again for your guidance. Hope you have a great weekend!

analysis.insight_summary: The main topic centers on software freezing during upload/download operations between the user's computer and the controller module using [product_name] V6.1.12 and a USB cable. Initial confusion about compatibility with Windows 7 leads to troubleshooting, but the root cause is identified as an incorrect COM port selection. After manually setting the correct port in the software, the issue is resolved, allowing use on both Windows XP and Windows 7 systems.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects reliable operation of [product_name] for uploading and downloading via USB on compatible computers, without needing manual corrections or troubleshooting. Clear support and instructions regarding hardware and software compatibility are also desired.
